items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are named together.
Great accomplishment is included with them.
Becoming dear to the yoginīs is the stated result.
items.inference: One who attains enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment may become dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment.

items.question: Where did the ninth chapter of this teaching emerge?
premises: The chapter is identified as the ninth.
It is described as having emerged.
Its emergence is located in Candra-dvīpa.
items.inference: The ninth chapter emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self while surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire.
The self is described as standing.
The stance is on one foot.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What determination of knowledge is requested to be made manifest today?
premises: The speaker addresses the god.
The determination of knowledge is the topic.
Its manifestation is requested for today.
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make manifest today the determination of knowledge.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of the eight octads is sought to be known fully?
premises: The division concerns eight octads.
Full knowledge of it is desired.
The knowing is described as endless.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.
uncertainties: anantathā may qualify the extent or manner of the division rather than the knowing
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is the wheel in the secret place quickly accomplished, O Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is mentioned.
A wheel is located there.
Quick accomplishment of that wheel is asked about.
items.inference: The question seeks the means by which the wheel in the secret place is quickly accomplished.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, how is the wheel in the secret place quickly accomplished?

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the question asked by the great goddess?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval.
He addresses the great goddess.
He states he was asked about something hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the question because it concerns a matter difficult even for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and the forehead?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra state.
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead.
Both assignments are stated together.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa belongs to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ belongs to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed in the heart.
These placements are given in sequence.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa belongs to the throat region and the syllable śa belongs to the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What follows after the place-wheels have been declared to the beloved?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Their meditation is now offered as the topic.
The beloved is commanded to listen.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad to be visualized?
premises: The lotus is described as divine.
It has eight spokes or petals.
It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The divine lotus should be visualized as eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
uncertainties: āra can mean spoke or petal in lotus imagery
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with an equal mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal mind.
Village dharma is named as something to abandon.
Abandonment is prescribed.
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equal mind should abandon village dharma.
uncertainties: grāma-dharma may refer to conventional social or household duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equal mind, one should abandon the ways of village life.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice regarding distant hearing and bonds?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned.
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned.
Both are presented as related attainments.
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobha may mean arresting or stunning bonds/obstacles
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly attributed to this yogic practice?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is named as an attainment.
The statement is given in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the practice grants immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may refer to bodily or situational transformation
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized in meditation?
premises: The wheel is identified as the second.
It has eight petals.
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled wheel, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
The practitioner makes forms.
These forms are made in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power does the practitioner possess when overcome by anger?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry.
The object of destruction is the entire triple world.
The triple world includes moving and unmoving beings.
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he may destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: The wheel is identified as the third great wheel.
It is described as a liberator.
Its liberating scope concerns nine principles.
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned.
Seeing from very far away is mentioned.
Both are presented as resulting powers.
items.inference: The practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the power to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the power to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a solitary practitioner intent on meditation manifest multiple forms?
premises: The practice is done in solitude.
The practitioner is intent on meditation.
Making many forms is commanded.
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, the practitioner should manifest forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, make forms in many ways.

items.question: What result comes to one intent on constant practice of this discipline?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice.
Immortality is stated as the result.
The result is asserted emphatically.
items.inference: One intent on constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified.
Death from aging is the object concerned.
A future overcoming is stated.
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.
uncertainties: nāśanena may mean fasting or absence of eating; gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ is idiomatic for going beyond death
items.plain_english: By not eating during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What youthful form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: The means is constant practice through yoga.
A duration of two times eight years is specified.
A resulting form is promised.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is taken as the form of a sixteen-year-old
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from always contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is to be contemplated.
The contemplation is to be done always.
Shaking the triple world is stated as the result.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
uncertainties: the object contemplated as smoke-colored may be the wheel, deity, or self
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
